s1.explanation: The unit responds to a single road vehicle with a long, low, car-like body seen whole from the side or in three-quarter view, parked on pavement. It is strongest for older or classic vehicles from about the 1950s to the 1980s, such as a 50s pickup, an old wagon or an old tanker lorry, and somewhat stronger for red bodies. It is weak for tall boxy vehicles like buses, minibuses and ambulances, for modern trucks, for rear views, for cluttered scenes with many vehicles, and for interiors. The ibex response suggests a general sensitivity to an elongated body in side profile.

s2.explanation: The unit responds to a single real road vehicle, especially a car or pickup, seen in clear side or three-quarter profile. In these views the long horizontal body, side windows and both wheels are visible. It also fires on other side-profile subjects, such as an old tanker truck and a standing ibex. Activity is highest for boxy, classic-looking sedans, wagons and pickups, often red. It drops for front-on views, close-ups, toys and models (Lego, cake, toy truck), cluttered scenes with many vehicles, larger buses or vans, and interiors.

s3.explanation: Responds to a single real road vehicle seen whole from the side or front three-quarter, with its long body and wheels filling the frame. It is strongest for boxy 1950s–1980s cars, wagons and trucks shot in a parking lot or on a road. It is weak for crowded scenes with many small vehicles, rear views, toy or model vehicles, very old 1920s–30s hot-rod shapes, and vehicle interiors. It also fires on horned ibex in side profile, possibly because of the long horizontal body on legs.
